title: Self-reporting Scaffolds for 3-Dimensional Cell Culture
protocol: Reconstitute 5-(and-6)-carboxyfluorescein, succinimidyl ester (FAM-SE) in dimethylformamide (DMF).
Reconstitute 6-carboxytetramethylrhodamine, succinimidyl ester (TAMRA-SE) in DMF.
Add 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES) to each reconstituted dye solution.
Stir the mixtures under a dry nitrogen atmosphere for 24 hours at 21 °C, protected from light.
Mix equal volumes of FAM-SE and TAMRA-SE with ethanol and ammonium hydroxide.
Add tetraethylorthosilicate (TEOS) to the dye mixture and continue stirring for an additional 2 hours.
Collect the nanosensors by rotary evaporation.
Store the collected nanosensors in a glass vial at 4 °C.
Prepare Sørensen's phosphate buffer solutions ranging from pH 5.5-8.0 using sodium phosphate monobasic and dibasic stock solutions.
Check the final pH of each buffer solution with a pH meter.
Adjust the pH of the buffer solutions if necessary using sodium hydroxide or hydrochloric acid.
Suspend the pH nanosensors in the pH buffers (5 mg/ml) by holding the vessel containing the nanosensor solution on a vortex for 3 min.
Submerge the vessel in an ultrasonicator until the solution becomes cloudy, approximately 5 minutes.
Repeat these steps to fully suspend the nanosensors in solution.
Place the first solution into an optical cuvette and use excitation wavelengths of 488 nm for FAM and 568 nm for TAMRA.
Collect emission wavelengths at 500-530 nm for FAM and 558-580 nm for TAMRA using a fluorescence spectrometer.
Change the solutions in the optical cuvette so that the pH can be observed at different pH values.
Continue collecting the emission spectra.
Calculate the ratio of the emission maxima produced at each pH value to produce a calibration curve.
Place a sample of the nanosensors onto a carbon coated electron microscope stub and sputter coat with gold for 5 min under an argon atmosphere.
Observe by scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
During imaging adjust the working distance, voltage and magnification to minimize electron charging.
Distance the needle tip 20 cm away from a 20 cm x 15 cm aluminum collecting plate.
Attach the electrode of a high voltage power supply to the tip of the syringe and the earth to the aluminum collecting plate.
Deliver the solution using a constant flow rate of 3.5 m/hr at 12 kV for 2 hr.
Leave the scaffold in a fume hood for 24 hr to allow solvent residue to evaporate.
Suspend nanosensors in the PLGA solution with ultrasonication for approximately 5 min.
Place a sample of the PLGA scaffold or pH responsive scaffold onto a carbon coated electron microscope stub.
Immerse a sample of pH responsive scaffold into appropriate buffer solutions.
Cut the PLGA or pH responsive PLGA scaffolds into 2 cm² pieces.
Irradiate scaffolds with ultraviolet (UV) light for 15 min each side at a distance of 8 cm.
Transfer irradiated scaffolds to a 12-well culture plate and place a steel ring on top.
Add a solution of Penicillin/Streptomycin (5% v/v) in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) inside and outside the steel ring.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C with 5% CO₂.
Remove sterilizing solution from scaffolds.
Wash scaffolds with PBS.
Add cell culture media to the inside and outside of the steel ring (500 μl each).
Place scaffolds in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO₂) whilst preparing a cell suspension.
Prepare a cell suspension using Trypan Blue exclusion assay.
Create a cell suspension to achieve a concentration of 1 x 10⁶ cells/ml.
Remove media from the inside and outside of the steel ring.
Replace with prewarmed cell culture media on the outside of the steel ring.
Add 300 μl of the cell suspension to the inside of the steel ring - rock plate backwards and forwards gently to distribute cells.
Place the cell culture plate into an incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Refresh the media every 2-3 days as required by the experiment duration.
Seed cells onto PLGA scaffold as described in section 3.1.
Wash the cells with PBS before nanosensor delivery.
Change the media from standard culture media to antibiotic and serum-free media.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 1 hour prior to nanosensor delivery.
Prepare the nanosensor-liposome complex by sonicating nanosensors (5 mg) with Optimem (50 μl).
Sonication should be brief.
Add Lipofectamine 2000 (5 µl) to Optimem (45 µl).
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 5 min.
Combine solution A with solution B containing Lipofectamine and Optimem.
Incubate the combined solutions at room temperature for 20 min to form solution C.
Add 100 μl of solution C to cells.
Incubate the cells with solution C at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 3 hours.
Remove cell-seeded scaffolds from the incubator.
Aspirate media and wash twice with PBS.
Add 1 ml of PBS to allow live cell visualization by confocal microscopy.
Immerse the cell-seeded scaffold into buffers of different pH.
Monitor the pHi by determining the ratio of fluorescence intensities from FAM and TAMRA using confocal microscopy.
Dilute LysoTracker Red stock solution to 50 nM.
Add 2 µl of diluted LysoTracker Red solution to cells cultured on PLGA scaffolds.
Incubate the cells with LysoTracker Red for 1 hr at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Remove the media from the cells after incubation.
Wash the cells twice with PBS (pH 7.4).
Change the media to PBS (pH 7.4) (2 ml).
Add nuclear stain Draq5 to the PBS to achieve a final concentration of 5 µM.
Incubate the cells with Draq5 for 3 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Excite the FAM only nanosensors using a 488 nm argon laser.
Observe fluorescence at 500-530 nm for FAM only nanosensors.
Excite LysoTracker Red with a 568 nm krypton laser.
Observe fluorescence at 580-600 nm for LysoTracker Red.
Excite Draq5 with a 633 nm helium/neon laser.
Observe fluorescence at 650-750 nm for Draq5.
